land.text: Bagirmi, southeast of Lake Chad around Massenya north of the Chari river

successors.note: Became a French protectorate "after the signing of a treaty in 1897", a colony in 1902 (Bagirmi Sultanate page); the sultanate survives as a non-sovereign monarchy in Chad.

capitals.name: Massenya
capitals.note: "Its capital was Massenya, north of the Chari River"; the page gives no capital moves. Rabih burnt Massenya in 1893 and Wadai partly destroyed it in 1870; the infobox names Chekna for 1893-1897.

correction.text: Bagirmi, southeast of Lake Chad around Massenya north of the Chari river

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Bagirmi row). The kingdom "emerged from a group of chiefdoms around 1522"; some king lists date its founder Abd al-Mahmud Begli to 1493-1503. The page gives no area: southeast of Lake Chad, the gazetteer region Baguirmi (the Chari-Baguirmi region) stands for it.

keyframe_review.note: Under Mbang Burkumanda (1635-1665) Bagirmi "extended its influence north to Lake Chad"; drawn as the Hadjer-Lamis shore at confidence 1. The page also says Bagirmi was a tributary of Bornu for much of its existence (from Alooma's reign, 1571-1602/3, until independence under Muhammad al-Amin, 1751-1785), and of Wadai after 1805: those are Bagirmi's own status and are not shown here.

wars.name: Bornu conquest of Bagirmi
wars.outcome: Bornu under Idris Alooma (1571-1602/3) "embarked on conquering its smaller southern neighbours"; Bagirmi was a tributary of Bornu for much of its existence and regained independence under Muhammad al-Amin (1751-1785).
wars.note: No border change is dated; the Bornu dossier (empire-of-kanem) does not draw Bagirmi.

zones.text: Bagirmi, southeast of Lake Chad around Massenya north of the Chari river

wars.outcome: In 1805 Wadai sacked Massenya and killed the mbang; Wadai invaded again in 1870 and partly destroyed Massenya.

wars.name: Rabih's conquest of Bagirmi

zones.text: Bagirmi, southeast of Lake Chad around Massenya north of the Chari river

wars.outcome: Rabih defeated a joint Bagirmi-Wadai army in 1892 and, in 1893 (Bagirmi page), conquered Baguirmi and burnt Massenya; Bagirmi accepted a French protectorate in 1897 and the French and Bagirmi killed Rabih in 1900.
wars.note: The Rabih page has the defeat of Gaourang II's Massenya rule in 1892; the Bagirmi page has 1893.

certainty.note: No frontier is described; Bagirmi was a core around Massenya whose tributary relations with Bornu and Wadai changed over time.

notes:
Bagirmi Sultanate, additions batch af-03-x; no Cliopatria row. Pages: Bagirmi Sultanate, Rabih az-Zubayr (2 of the budget).

Conflicts: founder Mbang Birni Besse (1522) versus Abd al-Mahmud Begli (1493-1503), start 1522 (infobox and text); Rabih's conquest of Massenya 1892 (Rabih page: after defeating a joint Bagirmi-Wadai army) versus 1893 (Bagirmi page), 1893 followed; the infobox lists mbang reigns 1522-1536, 1885-1912 and a successor/predecessor "Chekna" 1893-1897 that the text does not explain. The Wadai dossier (af-03-b) records the 1805 sack as a one-year contest with "no occupation or tribute described afterwards" while the Bagirmi page says Wadai "made Bagirmi a tributary": a vassal_start for Bagirmi under Wadai from 1805 (and under Bornu, for most of 1571-1751) would belong in those two dossiers; the date the tribute to Bornu ended is the page's "Muhammad al-Amin (1751-1785)".

No area on any page; the 1635 extension to Lake Chad is influence (confidence 1). Rulers: only fragments on the page; no strip.

Counterparts: state-of-rabih-az-zubayr (written in this batch). Gazetteer: Massenya (place; coordinates 11.40 N, 16.17 E taken from general knowledge as a point, not from the page); Chekna.
